What it would do differently

The leads the player wrote, each with where it happened and what would settle it. An ask is a link into the replay above.

  1. A down staircase is on a square with three adjacent walls

    — a corridor end — and there are three or four of them per level, at least 16 tiles apart. I checked every dead end I found on depth 1 and none of them had one, which is the expected result of covering sixty squares of 13,068.

    What would settle it: a run that walks only corridor ends and reports where the '>' actually appears, and how many dead ends there are per down staircase — if most dead ends are not staircases, the "look for the three walls" heuristic is weaker than it sounds.

  2. The town-and-depth-1 shuttle is worth testing properly.

    Every descent from the town builds a new depth 1 with new monsters, and on the two fresh levels I saw the monsters were 1-experience mice while the depth-1 table promises small kobolds at 5 and soldier ants at 3.

    What would settle it: a run that descends, kills what is beside the staircase and comes back up, counting the kills per ask and the experience per kill, and says where the good monsters actually are.

  3. The mouse tax is measurable.

    One 38-digit walk cost 22 hit points.

    What would settle it: the same walk taken with the monster killed behind you before each step, which I believe would cost almost nothing.

  4. Whether a Priest's spell failure is ever zero.

    The list says 5%.

    What would settle it: cast a level-1 prayer twenty times and count.

- TO-HIT, measured from the source (src/player-attack.c chance_of_missile_hit_base + hit_chance): BTH_PLUS_ADJ is 3, so the sheet's 'To-hit 20' for melee and '12' for shooting are the raw skill divided by 3. The RAW numbers are what the roll uses: my throw skill = Dwarf 0 + Priest 35 = 35, so a thrown flask of oil has to-hit 35 MINUS THE DISTANCE to the target. At one tile that is 34, which beats AC 24 (a small kobold) at about 56 per cent. Against AC 36 (Grip, Fang, the large white snake) at one tile it is about 36 per cent. So oil can hurt the armoured monsters, and the distance penalty is the thing to manage. hit_chance is 12% + 83%*(to-hit - 2*AC/3)/to-hit, with a 5% always-miss floor. (ask 12)
- PRIST MELEE IS HOPELESS, from the source: calc_blows() divides adj_str_blow[STR] * class strength-multiplier by max(weapon weight, class min-weight). A Priest has strength-multiplier 3 and min-weight 35, so str_index is 0 for every weapon and the blow table gives exactly 100 energy per blow = 1.0 blow per turn, whatever I hold. My mace is 1d1+2, so melee is about 3 damage a turn against 22 for a flask of oil. THE ATTACK FOR THIS CLASS IS THROWN OIL, and the spell I was given by the random draw was Call Light (learned at ask 12) - which is src/effect-handler-general.c effect_handler_LIGHT_AREA: light_room(player->grid, true), it lights the WHOLE ROOM whatever the dice say, which is worth a lot with a torch's 3x3 view. - EXPLORATION SPEED: lxg moved exactly ONE tile on a fresh level, and minimaxflash-2 measured the same (lxg 3,3,12,1 tiles on four levels) while minimaxflash-1.4 measured 17 to 44 tiles for a LONG aim. The two are the same mechanism (find_path sets only_known = known(start) AND known(dest), so an UNKNOWN destination takes the unknown-is-passable fallback, and patched_distances_to_path() rebuilds a path backwards from a destination whose distance was never set) - the difference is that the NEAREST unknown square gives a bogus short path and a FAR one gives a real route. So aim long, 30 to 70 tiles, and in free mode (p) so the digits move the cursor one tile each. (ask 36)

- DIGGING, from the source: walking INTO a diggable wall tunnels it (cmd-cave.c, the walk command calls do_cmd_tunnel_aux on square_isdiggable squares), so a digit string of south steps is many digging attempts in ONE ask - and the ask budget is turns-independent. calc_digging_chances(): QUARTZ = (skill-20)*2 = 40 of 1200 = 3.3 per cent an attempt, MAGMA = (skill-10)*4 = 120 = 10 per cent, GRANITE = (skill-40)*1 = 0, so a Dwarf with digging 40 can dig quartz and magma but never granite. '*' is drawn for both MAGMA_K and QUARTZ_K, veins with treasure, and digging one places gold. (ask 50)
- THE DIG REPEATS ITSELF: do_cmd_tunnel_aux returns more=true on a failed dig, so the walk command into a diggable wall keeps digging turn after turn until the wall is gone - one key press can be thirty digging attempts. If that is true the game will be digging between my asks, which costs no asks at all. A Dwarf is the only class here that can do this at all (Warrior skill-dig:0). (ask 51)
- WALKING INTO A WALL NEVER DIGS: do_cmd_walk_test() refuses every non-passable square ('There is a wall in the way!'), so the dig must be the T command with a direction. do_cmd_tunnel() takes the direction, calls do_cmd_tunnel_aux(), and 'if (!more) disturb(player)' - more is true on a failed dig, so the tunnel command REPEATS on its own until the wall is gone or the chance is zero. One keypress, many turns, no extra asks. (ask 52)
- MY DIGGING SKILL: calc_bonuses gives SKILL_DIGGING = race 40 (Dwarf) + adj_str_dig[STR 18] = 9 + weapon_weight/10 = 12 for the 12 lb Mace, so 61 - and the chances are out of 1200: rubble 488 (41%), magma 204 (17%), quartz 82 (6.8%), granite 21 (1.75%). So 100 attempts failing points at a granite-class vein. The turn counter rose by 1000 during one 'T2', which is 100 player actions (the game's turn counter advances by TEN per action) - so the tunnel command really did repeat itself. (ask 53)

The town has one street that crosses it - row 11, open from column 3 to column 58 - and every store can be reached from it. (ask 64)
- THE TOWN AIMS WALK ONE TILE AND STOP - three different aims in the town all moved me one tile (to a store tile, to a store tile again, and to (7,11) thirty-seven tiles away). The digit strings work. I do not know why the town's pathfinder behaves this way and the game source was not enough to say; the observation stands on its own. (ask 65)
- The town is full of harmless townsfolk: I walked into a village idiot, which fled in terror, and the walk stopped there. They are the 't' glyph (monster_base.txt: base townsfolk, SPIRIT | CLEAR_WEB) and the 'C'. (ask 66)
- BUYING IN THE ARMOURY: 'p' then the row letter then the quantity then Enter then any other key. The Armoury letters: a) Robes 14, c) Soft Leather Armours 84, f) Studded Leather 150, h) Leather Scale Mail 546, j) Wicker Shield 336, m) Metal Caps 24, n) Leather Gloves 6, o) Iron Shod Boots 176, q) Iron Shod Boots 84. (ask 67)
- BOUGHT: Soft Leather Armour [8,+0] for 84 of my 92 gold, 8 left. It is pack letter i. Wearing it should take my armour class from 3 (Robes +2, Gloves +1) to 9 if the Robes come off, or to 11 if they stack - and the Robes are body armour in this build (body.txt has no robe slot), so they should come off into the pack. (ask 68)
- 'Cur AC' is player->known_state.ac + known_state.to_a (ui-display.c:307) - the KNOWN state, not the true one, so it can lag behind a change of equipment. I need to see the equipment screen before I trust it. (ask 69)
- CUR AC 9 - the Soft Leather Armour is worn (g) On body, the Robes came off into the pack, the Leather Gloves are on my hands, the Wooden Torch has 4812 turns left, and the mace is 2d4 (the birth sheet's 'Melee 1d1,+2' was wrong: a Mace is 2d4, so a blow is 4 to 10 damage, not 3). The 'Cur AC' line was STALE at 3 until the equipment screen was opened: it prints known_state.ac + known_state.to_a, and the known state only catches up when the equipment is looked at. (ask 70)
- TOWN EXIT: from the Armoury I walked north once and east along row 12 to column 42, then north to the staircase. The town is full of townfolk who interrupt walks and cost turns (a village idiot drooled on me) but they do almost no damage - except the 'C' one, which has taken 4 hit points off me over the shopping trip, and I do not know what it is yet. (ask 72)
- FRESH DEPTH 1, and the whole shopping trip cost me 4 hit points to a town monster of unknown kind. Now: AC 9, HP 12/14, SP 2/2, 18 flasks of oil, a Scroll of Phase Door, 2 Potions of Cure Serious Wounds, the brown potion (Cure Light Wounds), a Scroll of Word of Recall, the Robes in the pack, 8 gold. The up staircase here is in a 3x3 room with walls all round, so the exit is one of (31,11) or (35,11). (ask 73)
- THE MAP SHOWS THE WHOLE ROOM: I am in a room whose walls are at columns 31 and 42 and rows 7 and 15, and the map draws all of it - two giant white mice ('r', 2 hit points, AC 4, 1d2, experience 1, flags MULTIPLY) and two items ('!') at (35,9) and (31,10) - although my torch only lights three tiles. So Call Light, the one prayer I have, may be worth less to me than the map panel is. (ask 78)
- THE KEYPAD, again, because I got it wrong: the layout is 7 8 9 / 4 5 6 / 1 2 3, so 3 is down-RIGHT and 1 is down-LEFT, 8 is up, 2 is down, 4 is left, 6 is right. A string of '3's walks me SE, not west. (ask 80)
- FIVE GIANT WHITE MICE now, from one: the giant white mouse carries MULTIPLY and breeds while alive, and they are 2 hit points with AC 4 and 1d2 damage each. Five of them at one tile would be 5 to 10 damage a round against my 13 hit points. Two of my options: fight them in the one-wide corridor where only one can reach me at a time, or throw oil - but a throw needs a VISIBLE target and my torch lights only three tiles, so I can only throw at a mouse that has already come adjacent. (ask 81)
- MELEE IS FREE AND A STRING OF DIGITS IS SEVERAL ATTACKS: the mace is 2d4 blessed, so 4 to 10 damage, and a giant white mouse has 2 hit points - one blow kills it. '6' into a mouse attacks it instead of moving, and the string continues, so five digits is five attacks or moves in one ask. (ask 82)
- THE ORDER OF BLOWS IS IN MY FAVOUR: my blow happens before the monsters' in the same turn, so a mouse that dies from my blow never bites me. In a one-wide corridor only the mouse in front of me is adjacent, so the whole fight should cost about one hit point each, not five. (ask 83)
- Four mice slain for zero hit points - my blow comes first in the turn, so a mouse I kill never bites me. Eight experience in total, and CL2 needs twelve: four more mice. But they BREED: one mouse became seven in about fifteen turns, so I am killing them about as fast as they arrive. (ask 84)
- Eight mice now and my hit points are down to 6 of 14, so I have to heal before anything else. The Cure Serious Wounds is worth 70 gold and the brown potion 20, but at character level 1 both heal me only to 14, so the cheap one is the right one to spend - if the flavour analysis is right. I am quaffing the KNOWN Cure Serious Wounds rather than betting on my own reading of the flavour index with eight monsters in the room. (ask 86)
- THE QUAFF PROMPT NAMES ITS OWN LETTERS: 'q' printed 'Quaff which potion? (Inven: d-e, ESC)' with d) 2 Potions of Cure Serious Wounds and e) a Brown Potion - so the pack letters are d and e, not what I had guessed. The SAFE way to identify an unknown potion is the Alchemist's 'd' (sell): src/store.c do_cmd_sell() calls object_flavor_aware() and learns the runes before the item changes hands, so with selling off you get 0 gold, lose the item, and know the kind for the rest of the game. (ask 87)
- LEVEL 2 at last: HP 10/24, SP 2/4, AC 9, and 'You can learn 2 more prayers' - the priest gets a spell slot per level (adj_mag_study for a WIS of 18 is enough for two). Twelve experience so far, and CL3 needs thirty for this Dwarf. (ask 90)
- Eight mice, and I am at 8 of 24 hit points with the LOW HITPOINT WARNING up. Two of them are adjacent (north and south of me) and each will bite me for 1d2 while I kill the other. The narrow corridor is where only one can reach me at a time. (ask 92)
- CORRECTION TO MY OWN NOTEBOOK (ask 80): THE FLAVOUR NAME DOES NOT IDENTIFY THE KIND. src/obj-util.c flavor_assign() gives each kind a RANDOM unused flavour from its tval's pool - 'choice = randint0(flavor_count)' - so the 41 potion flavours are shuffled onto the 41 potion kinds, not assigned in file order. 'A Brown Potion' is therefore one of the 41 potions and the flavour tells me NOTHING: my 'flavour 200 = the eighth potion = Cure Light Wounds' was a plausible-sounding theory that the source refuses. The lesson fits the rest of this run: a number that looks like it must mean something is not evidence until the code says so. So the brown potion is an unknown, with the depth-1 pool's 16 per cent chance of being one of the harmful kinds, and I am spending the KNOWN potion instead. (ask 94)
- THE MICE ARE A TAX I CANNOT AFFORD: every ask I spend costs me about two hit points, so forty more asks of exploration would cost eighty hit points against a maximum of twenty-four. A run that keeps asking questions on a level with eight mice does not end with a character level, it ends with a death. The lesson for the page: count what a monster costs per ask before deciding to fight it - the number of asks left is the budget that matters. (ask 95)
- HEALED to 24/24 with the last Cure Serious Wounds. Now 54 asks left, 13 experience, 18 flasks, AC 9, and eight mice. The plan for the rest of the run: go up to the town on the up staircase (the monsters do not follow through stairs), learn the two prayers and cast each once there for the first-cast experience and for Bless (+5 AC) or Minor Healing (a free heal), buy two more flasks of oil with my 8 gold, and go down again to a FRESH depth 1 - where the monsters are small kobolds and soldier ants worth five and three experience each, instead of one-experience mice. (ask 96)
- THE ESCAPE THAT COSTS NO RISK: the Scroll of Phase Door teleports ten squares (object.txt dice:10) and the mice move at the same speed as I do (110), so after the jump they stay ten tiles behind and never reach me again, while I walk on. I am spending the scroll rather than the brown potion, because the potion is a sixteen per cent chance of poison damage every turn for ten to thirty turns, and the scroll is certain. (ask 99)
- I READ THE WRONG SCROLL: the pack letters MOVE when items are used up - I drank both Potions of Cure Serious Wounds, so the two scrolls shifted down one letter and 'f' was the Scroll of Word of Recall, not the Phase Door. The Recall is now READ and its timer is running (15 to 34 player actions), which I will use as my escape: teleport away with the Phase Door, then walk, and the Recall will fire and put me in the town. The Phase Door is now pack letter e. (ask 101)
- PHASE DOOR: ten squares, no damage taken, and the mice are now six tiles west of me while I am at column 40 - they move at the same speed as I do, so if I keep moving they never reach me. The Recall's timer is running (15 to 34 player actions from the moment I read it), and studying and casting are actions too, so I can spend the wait learning the two prayers I am owed at level 2: the priest takes a RANDOM prayer from the Novice's Handbook, and at character level 2 the learnable ones are Detect Evil, Minor Healing and Bless, because I already know Call Light and the book's other two need level 3 and level 5. (ask 102)
- Learned Minor Healing: 2 spell points, and it heals the caster for a level-dependent amount plus a percentage - at level 2 that is about 12 hit points, and it also cures 20 turns of stunning and cutting. That is my third heal and it costs no gold. (ask 103)
- Learned Bless as well: 2 spell points, and it gives +5 AC and +10 to-hit for a level-dependent number of turns (level + 10). At AC 9 that would be AC 14 while it lasts - and the priest's spell failures are all but nil, because class.txt gives the Priest player-flags ZERO_FAIL, so a priest never miscasts. (ask 104)
- THE CAST PROMPT IS TWO STAGES: 'm' asks 'Cast which book?' (the spell lives in the book, and the priest has only one) and then the spell list comes up with its own letters in the order the prayers were learned - a) Call Light, b) Minor Healing, c) Bless. (ask 105)
- Cast Minor Healing: the first cast of a spell pays its first-use experience, and this one paid 4 (NXT 12 after it, from 16). Minor Healing at level 2 healed 12 points - exactly the class.txt formula, level + 10 - which took me from 12 to 24. The spell list letters are not the order I learned them: 'c' was Minor Healing, so Bless must be 'b'. And the spell costs 2 of my 4 spell points, so Bless waits until the points regenerate. (ask 106)
- THE MICE COST MORE THAN I THOUGHT: a 38-digit walk along the corridor cost 22 hit points, because the ones behind me bite every turn they are adjacent. The lessons are that a corridor fight is only free if I kill the one behind me as it arrives, and that a level with a breeding monster is a per-ask tax of one to two hit points, which no budget of 50 asks can pay at 24 hit points. The brown potion is a sixteen per cent chance of poison and an eighty-four per cent chance of a heal, and the alternative to quaffing it is certain death, so I quaff it. (ask 107)
- THE BROWN POTION WAS A POTION OF SPEED - the flavour name really did say nothing about the kind, exactly as src/obj-util.c flavor_assign() says it must (it hands the flavours out at random). And it is a good one: Speed gives +10 to my speed, so I now move faster than the mice at 110 and they can never catch me again. I am at 2 of 24 hit points, so what I need now is the town, and the Scroll of Word of Recall is still counting down. (ask 108)
- THE WORD OF RECALL TOOK ME TO THE TOWN AND DID NOT HEAL ME: I am still at 2 of 24 hit points, so minimaxflash-1-again's 'arriving in town healed me from 28/33 to 33/33' was a REST in the town, not the Recall itself. The Recall's timer is 15 to 34 player actions, and it fired after about thirty - which is why it interrupted my walk and dropped me in the town with the message 'There is a wall in the way!'. (ask 109)
- THE TOWN IS ALMOST EMPTY NOW: one monster left, a boil-covered wretch one tile south of me, and it woke up and interrupted my rest. It has 2 hit points and my blessed mace does 4 to 10, so one blow kills it, and then the town is quiet enough to rest in. Resting is the only way to get my 21 missing hit points back - the Scroll of Recall did not heal me at all. (ask 110)
- The Potion of Speed wore off after about 170 turns ('You feel yourself slow down'), which is a useful number: the Speed effect is long enough to outrun anything on the level for a couple of hundred turns. The rest healed four hit points in sixteen actions before it was interrupted, which is about a quarter of my maximum per ten actions. (ask 111)
- A SECOND 'R' AFTER A REST OPENED THE KNOWLEDGE MENU ('~' - Items, Action commands, Manage items, Information, Utility, Hidden), so a rest prompt that has already been answered does not swallow the next key the way I expected. One command per ask is the rule that holds everywhere in this game. (ask 112)
- Fully healed in the town: 24 of 24 hit points and 4 of 4 spell points, and no monsters in the town at all now. The spell list is in alphabetical order, so it is a) Bless, b) Call Light, c) Minor Healing - and 'c' being Minor Healing is what fixed the order for me. (ask 113)
- The spell list is a) Call Light, b) Bless, c) Minor Healing - not alphabetical and not the order I learned them (Call Light, Minor Healing, Bless). I measured it: 'a' gave Call Light and 'c' gave Minor Healing, so 'b' is Bless. Call Light was not a waste: it lights the whole room, which is how I see a room's contents with a torch that lights three tiles. (ask 114)
- THE SPELL LIST SHOWS THE WHOLE BOOK, not only what I know, in the order class.txt lists it: a) Call Light, b) Detect Evil, c) Minor Healing, d) Bless, e) Sense Invisible (level 3), f) Heroism (level 5). The Fail column reads 5 per cent for the level-1 prayers and 9 per cent for Bless - so a Priest's spells are NOT failure-free in this build. class.txt's player-flags ZERO_FAIL only means the failure rate is not floored at 5 per cent for everyone else; the priest's own floor is adj_mag_fail for WIS 18, which is 5. (ask 115)
- BLESS CAST: 'You feel righteous!' - +5 armour class and +10 to-hit for a level-dependent number of turns, so my AC 9 becomes AC 14 for as long as it lasts, and the first cast paid 4 experience. The list is the whole book in class.txt order, so the letters are fixed for the rest of the game: a Call Light, b Detect Evil, c Minor Healing, d Bless, e Sense Invisible, f Heroism. (ask 116)
- A SLIP OF THE KEYPAD: '4' is LEFT and '6' is RIGHT, and I sent '4444' intending east, so I walked into the wall west of me and nothing happened. Cur AC 14 confirmed (Bless), HP 24/24, NXT 3 - so the first cast of Bless paid 4 experience, and 27 of the 30 a Dwarf needs for level 3 is in. (ask 117)
- FRESH DEPTH 1 AGAIN, with AC 14 from Bless, 24 of 24 hit points, 27 experience (three short of level 3 for a Dwarf), 18 flasks of oil and one spell point. Thirty-two asks left. The up-staircase room here is a three-by-three box in my light radius; the exit has to be further out, and the map only holds what I have seen. (ask 118)
- THE CORRIDOR-END STRATEGY: the game puts each down staircase on a square with THREE adjacent walls - a corridor end - and keeps them at least 16 tiles apart (src/gen-util.c alloc_stairs), so a corridor end is the shape to look for and I can see it on the map without spending an ask. Walking to the end of a corridor and reading the map is the cheapest way to find a staircase. (ask 120)
- Twenty-four asks left. The M map is the only way to look at the WHOLE remembered level at once, and it costs one ask; the main panel only shows what is near me. Its priority array keeps a remembered staircase's cell (both LESS and MORE carry priority 25, the highest of any terrain), so a '>' cannot be hidden by the scaling. (ask 124)
- Seventeen asks left, and every corridor end I have found on this level is a dead end WITHOUT a staircase, which is what I expected: three or four down staircases on 198 by 66 squares is a lottery, and I have covered about sixty squares of the level. The M map is the last cheap check for a staircase I walked past but cannot see from here. (ask 129)
- The M map shows no down staircase anywhere in what I have remembered, and my remembered blob is about sixty level squares of the 198 by 66 level - the level is three screens wide and I have covered a corridor's worth of one corner of it. The corridor east of me is blocked by a quartz vein, and a Dwarf can dig quartz (skill 61 gives 82 of 1200, about seven per cent an attempt), so one 'T6' is a hundred attempts for the price of one ask. (ask 130)
- THE M VIEW EATS THE NEXT KEY: my 'T6' went to the map display and only the '6' reached the game, which is why I got 'There is a wall in the way!' instead of a dig. The same thing happened earlier with the store: a screen that is a menu takes your first key. (ask 131)
- Bless has expired (Cur AC back to 9), and the spell points have regenerated to 4 of 4. Two experience short of level 3. The vein and granite wall east of the corridor is five tiles thick at least, and a down staircase behind it would be a lucky break rather than a likely one. (ask 144)

note: BIRTH: the random race drew a DWARF, and the class menu's third column proves it: Hit die 13 = Dwarf race hitdie 11 + Priest class hitdie 2, and the stat column (Str +1, Int -6, Wis +5, Dex -3, Con +3) is exactly Dwarf 2:-3:2:-2:2 plus Priest -1:-3:3:-1:1. Dwarf facts from p_race.txt: stats 2:-3:2:-2:2, skill-dig:40 (a Dwarf can dig, unlike a Warrior), exp:120, infravision 5, obj-flags:PROT_BLIND (immune to blindness - which is one of the ways the manual says a Priest dies), player-flags:SEE_ORE. CON mod +3 means CON stat 20, and adj_con_mhp[20] = 200, so +2 hit points per level - the best constitution any Priest can have. The race menu's letters really are a,b,c,d,e,f,g,i,m,n,o (h,j,k,l skipped). (ask 4)

note: TO-HIT, measured from the source (src/player-attack.c chance_of_missile_hit_base + hit_chance): BTH_PLUS_ADJ is 3, so the sheet's 'To-hit 20' for melee and '12' for shooting are the raw skill divided by 3. The RAW numbers are what the roll uses: my throw skill = Dwarf 0 + Priest 35 = 35, so a thrown flask of oil has to-hit 35 MINUS THE DISTANCE to the target. At one tile that is 34, which beats AC 24 (a small kobold) at about 56 per cent. Against AC 36 (Grip, Fang, the large white snake) at one tile it is about 36 per cent. So oil can hurt the armoured monsters, and the distance penalty is the thing to manage. hit_chance is 12% + 83%*(to-hit - 2*AC/3)/to-hit, with a 5% always-miss floor. (ask 12)

note: PRIST MELEE IS HOPELESS, from the source: calc_blows() divides adj_str_blow[STR] * class strength-multiplier by max(weapon weight, class min-weight). A Priest has strength-multiplier 3 and min-weight 35, so str_index is 0 for every weapon and the blow table gives exactly 100 energy per blow = 1.0 blow per turn, whatever I hold. My mace is 1d1+2, so melee is about 3 damage a turn against 22 for a flask of oil. THE ATTACK FOR THIS CLASS IS THROWN OIL, and the spell I was given by the random draw was Call Light (learned at ask 12) - which is src/effect-handler-general.c effect_handler_LIGHT_AREA: light_room(player->grid, true), it lights the WHOLE ROOM whatever the dice say, which is worth a lot with a torch's 3x3 view. (ask 13)

note: AIM MUST BE IN FREE MODE: src/ui-target.c, a direction key in the DEFAULT 'interesting' mode picks the next interesting GRID (target_get_monsters), not the next tile - so '*33332g' snapped the cursor to the town leper and walked to it, and '*996666g' found no interesting grid and walked nowhere. Pressing 'p' inside the targeting mode sets show_interesting=false and focuses the player; only then does a digit move the cursor one tile. The town is 66x22 (constants.txt town-wid/town-hgt) and the map panel is 66x22, so in town the panel coordinates ARE the level coordinates and never scroll. tools/screen/aim.py is wrong on this and I will fix it. note: EXPLORATION SPEED: lxg moved exactly ONE tile on a fresh level, and minimaxflash-2 measured the same (lxg 3,3,12,1 tiles on four levels) while minimaxflash-1.4 measured 17 to 44 tiles for a LONG aim. The two are the same mechanism (find_path sets only_known = known(start) AND known(dest), so an UNKNOWN destination takes the unknown-is-passable fallback, and patched_distances_to_path() rebuilds a path backwards from a destination whose distance was never set) - the difference is that the NEAREST unknown square gives a bogus short path and a FAR one gives a real route. So aim long, 30 to 70 tiles, and in free mode (p) so the digits move the cursor one tile each. (ask 36)

note: DIGGING, from the source: walking INTO a diggable wall tunnels it (cmd-cave.c, the walk command calls do_cmd_tunnel_aux on square_isdiggable squares), so a digit string of south steps is many digging attempts in ONE ask - and the ask budget is turns-independent. calc_digging_chances(): QUARTZ = (skill-20)*2 = 40 of 1200 = 3.3 per cent an attempt, MAGMA = (skill-10)*4 = 120 = 10 per cent, GRANITE = (skill-40)*1 = 0, so a Dwarf with digging 40 can dig quartz and magma but never granite. '*' is drawn for both MAGMA_K and QUARTZ_K, veins with treasure, and digging one places gold. (ask 50)

note: WALKING INTO A WALL NEVER DIGS: do_cmd_walk_test() refuses every non-passable square ('There is a wall in the way!'), so the dig must be the T command with a direction. do_cmd_tunnel() takes the direction, calls do_cmd_tunnel_aux(), and 'if (!more) disturb(player)' - more is true on a failed dig, so the tunnel command REPEATS on its own until the wall is gone or the chance is zero. One keypress, many turns, no extra asks. (ask 52)

note: CHEST TRAPS, from chest_trap.txt: a level-1 chest can carry the POISON GAS (poisoned for 10+d20 turns) or a POISON NEEDLE (1d4 damage and a permanent loss of STR or CON); the summoning runes (level 15) and the 5d8 exploding device (level 25) are out of reach at depth 1. So the chest at (12,19) is a real risk to a character with 14 hit points and no spare potions: poisoned for 30 turns stops my regeneration, and a STR loss costs me the weight allowance. I am leaving it and saying so. (ask 59)

note: SHOPPING DECISION, settled: 92 gold buys the Soft Leather Armour at 84 and 2 flasks of oil at 6, and I keep 2 gold. The reasoning that settled it: with about 80 asks left after the town trip I can kill perhaps 8 to 12 monsters at 4 to 8 asks each, so I need 10 to 20 flasks and no more - 20 is what I will have - and the extra 20 flasks the armour costs would never be spent. What I cannot afford is the hit rate: a depth-1 monster with to-hit 12 hits my AC 3 on 95 per cent of turns and my AC 9 on 53 per cent, and I have 14 hit points. (ask 60)

note: CORRECTION TO MY OWN NOTEBOOK (ask 80): THE FLAVOUR NAME DOES NOT IDENTIFY THE KIND. src/obj-util.c flavor_assign() gives each kind a RANDOM unused flavour from its tval's pool - 'choice = randint0(flavor_count)' - so the 41 potion flavours are shuffled onto the 41 potion kinds, not assigned in file order. 'A Brown Potion' is therefore one of the 41 potions and the flavour tells me NOTHING: my 'flavour 200 = the eighth potion = Cure Light Wounds' was a plausible-sounding theory that the source refuses. The lesson fits the rest of this run: a number that looks like it must mean something is not evidence until the code says so. So the brown potion is an unknown, with the depth-1 pool's 16 per cent chance of being one of the harmful kinds, and I am spending the KNOWN potion instead. (ask 94)
